TWO CORRECTIONS TO THE PYTEST GITHUB-ANNOTATION HOOK ON BRANCH codex/run-38005965478-1 (expected head e61b993; fail closed and write nothing if it moved). The spec example you were given was wrong about one escaping detail; this fixes it. Only tests/conftest.py and tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py may change.

CORRECTION 1 - message escaping. In github_failure_annotation, the MESSAGE part (after the final '::') must escape ONLY '%'->'%25', '\r'->'%0D', '\n'->'%0A'. Remove the extra .replace(':', '%3A') on the message; GitHub does not unescape %3A in the message, so colons would show literally as '%3A' in the Checks tab. Property values (file, line, title) keep the ',' and ':' escaping as they are now. Update test_call_failure_annotation_includes_location_and_assertion so the expected literal is '::error file=tests/test_x.py,line=42,title=call%3A tests/test_x.py%3A%3Atest_y::AssertionError: boom%0Aassert 1 == 2'. Add one assertion somewhere that a message containing ':' keeps the raw ':'.

CORRECTION 2 - keep the useful end of the traceback. pytest's longreprtext for a failed test starts with the traceback and ends with the 'E   AssertionError: ...' lines, so truncating to the FIRST 1000 characters can cut off the actual error. Change the hook (pytest_runtest_logreport) to build longrepr_text like this: crash = getattr(getattr(report, 'longrepr', None), 'reprcrash', None); head = str(crash.message) if crash is not None and getattr(crash, 'message', None) else ''; full = report.longreprtext or str(report.longrepr or ''); tail = full[-700:] if len(full) > 700 else full; longrepr_text = (head + '\n' + tail) if head and head not in tail else (tail or head). Keep github_failure_annotation's own 1000-char cap and ' ...' marker unchanged (it still applies after this). Also, when crash has a usable path and lineno (crash.path non-empty string, crash.lineno an int), pass location=(crash.path, crash.lineno - 1, report.location[2] if report.location else '') so the annotation points at the actual failing line; note crash.path may be absolute, so convert it to a path relative to the repository root (Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent) when it is inside the repo, otherwise keep report.location as before. Keep everything inside the existing try/except Exception: pass.

TESTS: extend tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py with (a) a hook test using a stand-in report whose longrepr has a reprcrash SimpleNamespace(path=<repo root>/'tests/test_x.py' as str, lineno=12, message='AssertionError: tail wins') and a longreprtext of 3000 chars that ends with 'E   AssertionError: tail wins'; under monkeypatch.setenv('GITHUB_ACTIONS','true') assert the single emitted line contains 'file=tests/test_x.py,line=12,' and contains 'AssertionError: tail wins' and does not contain the first 100 characters of the longreprtext; (b) the existing no-op test and the single-line test must still pass. Keep the existing module counter semantics (reset the counter in your new test via monkeypatch.setattr on the module globals so test order does not matter; add that reset to the existing hook tests too).

VALIDATION (paste commands and counts): 1. python -m pytest tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py tests/test_review_lab_v3.py -q -p no:cacheprovider  2. the throwaway probe again: create /tmp/annot_probe/test_probe.py containing `def test_boom():\n    assert 1 == 2`, run `GITHUB_ACTIONS=true python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider --rootdir=. -c pyproject.toml /tmp/annot_probe/test_probe.py -q` from the repo root, confirm exactly one line starts with '::error ' and contains 'AssertionError' with a raw ':' (not '%3A') and contains 'test_boom'; delete the probe afterwards  3. ruff check tests/conftest.py tests/test_ci_failure_annotations.py  4. git diff --name-only e61b993 lists only the two allowed files.
